review_note: Granted narrowly. Live Julia test test_gamma_animal_intercept_slope_sd.jl: 35 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips; the 108 manifest entries (DRModels.jl at 87a371a66, checked against a git archive of that commit) and the console-log sha256 match. Oracle: a base-R/Optim dense Laplace objective (_gamma_animal_intercept_slope_dense_laplace) with a hand-built non-unit-diagonal A (scaled AR-type R), a hand-built per-group SD vector exp(Z*alpha) for each of the two independent animal fields, a Gamma log-pdf from Distributions, and a Laplace logdet; it does not use the package likelihood. It is compared with fit.nll(theta) at the true parameters (atol 5e-3). Both members (animal intercept, with SD ~ z0, and animal slope, with SD ~ z1) are fitted jointly as independent fields (coef(intercept) and coef(x) selectors). My Totoro scratch run (Julia 1.10.12, DRModels.jl 87a371a66, taskset core 163) found fit.nll(theta) minus the oracle of 1.5e-12, and oracle gaps for emulated bugs of: swapped selectors z0/z1 31.3, reversed intercept SD 21.5, reversed slope SD 6.6, swapped alpha blocks 10.9, cov2cor(A) 4.9, 2A 9.4. All are at least about 1000 times the 5e-3 tolerance. The perturbations live in my scratch run, not in the test, so a later edit to the test could remove the protection without failing it. Row support is the slope member (q=1 per coefficient) of the intercept-plus-independent-slope animal fit, and the intercept is fitted jointly. The bridge (drm_bridge) comparison is only parity. Recovery in the test is loose (within 0.6). Does NOT establish: that the optimiser lands at the oracle optimum (the oracle is evaluated at the true theta, not at the fitted theta), recovery accuracy beyond one seed, a correlated intercept-slope block (the fields are independent), Ainv or pedigree input, native parity, or interval coverage.
